column1: # subjects.tsv — each project's subject: the version this harness was built
# from, and where a student downloads it.
# The subjects are 42's documents, so the public template does not carry them:
# each project folder there holds a SUBJECT-PLACEHOLDER.pdf instead, and this
# registry is what that page says. It names the project's page on the intranet
# (every language is reached from there), the version of the English subject
# the harness was built from, that PDF's SHA-256, and, where one is known, a
# direct link that serves exactly those bytes. A student who has a subject can
# tell whether it is the harness's version with `sha256sum en.subject.pdf`.
# One row per project: every module of tools/submit.sh's REMOTES table has one,
# and nothing else does. tools/subjects.sh reads the rows and checks them, and in
# the repository the subjects are tracked in, each project's en.subject.pdf must
# have its row's SHA-256, so a subject replaced without its row is reported
# (//tools:conventions, which also holds a project page that says "built from
# version X" to the row). In a clone of the template that check opens no
# subject: an en.subject.pdf there is the student's own, whatever its version.
# Columns, tab-separated:
#   project  the project folder, from the repo root
#   version  as the English subject's cover prints it ("Version: 13" is 13)
#   sha256   of that project's en.subject.pdf, 64 lowercase hex digits
#   page     the project's page on the intranet,
#            https://projects.intra.42.fr/projects/<slug>. It needs a 42 login,
#            and it offers the subject in the reader's own language
#   pdf      https://cdn.intra.42.fr/pdf/pdf/<id>/en.subject.pdf, checked to
#            serve exactly the bytes of sha256, or - where none is known: the
#            page of a group project shows no subject once it is over, and a
#            link 42 serves today for a revised subject is another version
#   checked  the day page and pdf were last checked, YYYY-MM-DD
# When a subject is replaced, its row changes with it: version, sha256, and pdf
# checked again against the new bytes (in a browser: the CDN refuses a client
# that is not one), or - .
